Internal helper: the frequency table from one or more jfreq() results

Source: R/tables.R
dot-jst_table_build_freq.Rd

Jeff's Table 2: each variable's label on a row of its own, its categories indented under it, then the style's frequencies columns – n and the percentage of all cases under apa. A variable with missing data closes on rows the missing.rows key chooses: combined, one Missing row, so each variable's rows add up to N and to 100 percent; each, a row per missing value by its label (its code where it has none; the label key's word for the cells left empty); none, no row. A category is named by its value label, or by its code where it has none, never by the printed string. Several results stack into one table; headings = and a named list of results put the variables under role headings, and markers = marks a variable's label row, as in the descriptives table. The general note opens on N when every variable comes from one pool of cases.

Usage

.jst_table_build_freq(
  results,
  style,
  headings = NULL,
  markers = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  note = NULL
)

Arguments

results

A list of jst_freq results; names are headings.

style

The style list.

headings

A named list: each heading's variables (or NULL).

markers

A named list: each specific note's variables (or NULL).

title

The user's title, or NULL for the type's template.

note

The user's general note, or NULL.

Value

A jst_table.
